newsitem.title: INDIA: Separatist tribals kill 17 Bengali Hindus in India.
newsitem.headline: Separatist tribals kill 17 Bengali Hindus in India.

text.p: Tribal militants shot dead at least 17 Bengali Hindus sleeping inside a market in remote northeastern India on Friday, local police said.
The separatist guerrillas, armed with automatic weapons, fired on several dozen people early in the morning in the marketplace of Kalyanpur town, Tripura state, then set houses on fire, they said.
Seventeen people died on the spot and at least 20 were seriously wounded in the attack at about 3 a.m. (2130 GMT), police in the state capital Agartala told Reuters by telephone.
One of the houses set on fire belonged to a member of the state assembly from the ruling Communist Party of India-Marxist, they said.
For two decades, guerrillas from indigenous tribes have been fighting for a separate state after the influx of large numbers of Bengali Hindus from Bangladesh, which neighbours the state to the west.
The tribals have lost their majority status to immigrant Bengali Hindus, who now make up about three-quarters of the state's population of 2.7 million.
About 10 tribal guerrilla groups operate in the state, which shares a 839 km (521 mile) border with Bangladesh. Officials say the militants have training camps in Bangladesh.
Authorities said it was the highest number of dead in insurgency-related violence since 1980, when 2,000 people were killed and 25,000 houses destroyed in riots between Bengalis and tribals.
"Tension between tribals and Bengalis has been rising for the last three to four years," a local intelligence official told Reuters in Guwahati, capital of neighbouring Assam state.
Security forces launched searches for the guerrillas, who authorities said were believed to have belonged to the National Liberation Front of Tripura.
